newFeatures: Import finishes as soon as every file is copied and checked: your photos appear right away, and ratings, keywords and edits from .xmp files fill in afterwards in the background. If you close LightBench, it carries on next time.
With RAW + JPEG pairs, the RAWs are imported first; the JPEGs follow and are stacked under them. You can close the Import window and let it continue in the background.
Two or three files are copied at once (every copy is still read back and checked, so it's safe to format the card).
New import option: "RAW only (skip JPEGs that have a RAW twin)".
Import steps are timed and recorded when Settings → Diagnostics → Record diagnostics is on, and the finished Import window shows a one-line summary.
bugFixes: A photo that was copied but never added to the library (for example after an interrupted import) now shows "Copied, not in library" in the Import window and is added without copying it again.
An empty file left by an interrupted copy is now replaced, instead of the new copy getting a "-1" name.

newFeatures: Library: when sorted by capture time, each day gets a heading (e.g. "Sunday, 19 October 2026 · 48 photos") that stays at the top while you scroll. A new View menu turns the headings off, or shows the date on each photo.
Import window: click a date to see only its photos, Ctrl-click to add more dates, Shift-click for a range. Each date shows how many of its photos are ticked, e.g. (12 / 48).
Import window: a "Stack each JPEG under its RAW" option (on by default), and Stacks › "Stack RAW + JPEG pairs" to stack pairs that are already in your library.
Develop: every group starts closed, and Advanced sections too. LightBench remembers which groups you open. Shortcuts and the jump bar still open their group.
Clearer labels throughout: settings are described by what they do, without references to other apps.
bugFixes: RAW files had their capture time shifted by your time zone's offset from UTC, so they could sort away from their JPEGs, appear under another date, or be copied into the next day's folder. Capture times are now read correctly, and RAWs already in your library are corrected once when the library is upgraded.
RAW + JPEG pairs are now stacked as soon as both files are imported (an interrupted import used to leave them unstacked), and pairs imported at different times are stacked too.

newFeatures: Settings → Diagnostics: turn on "Record diagnostics" to keep a log of what you do and how the app and graphics card respond. The log survives a crash or power-off; use "Export diagnostics…" to save it and share it. It never includes file names, folders or photos, and nothing is recorded while it's off.

Settings → Diagnostics shows which graphics card LightBench is using. If it's running on integrated Intel graphics, Develop shows a one-time tip on how to switch your browser to the faster graphics card in Windows.
bugFixes: The white balance picker no longer reprocesses the whole full-size photo just to draw its magnifier, which made it slow and used a lot of graphics memory. Picked values are unchanged.
Images replaced while you edit are now freed as soon as the drawings using them finish, instead of waiting for a moment when nothing is drawing.

newFeatures: Texture, Clarity and Dehaze in Basic → Presence. Texture brings out fine detail, Clarity the larger structures (mostly in the mid-tones), and Dehaze removes or adds haze. They're built on darktable's contrast & texture and haze removal. Clarity and Dehaze measure the cropped photo, so their look can shift a little when you re-crop.

A new Effects group: Post-crop vignette (Highlight Priority, Color Priority or Paint Overlay, with the centre and shape under Advanced), Grain (Amount, Size, Roughness; colour grain under Advanced) and Glow (Bloom, Diffusion or Halation, with Range, Spread and Warmth).
Masks can now use Texture, Clarity and Dehaze, and set how much Glow they get.
Export has a new "Dither JPEGs" option (off by default) that hides banding in smooth gradients such as vignettes.

Lightroom's Texture, Clarity, Dehaze, vignette and grain settings are read from and written to its .xmp files. Lightroom's Glow style and sliders are read but left switched off (the field for its amount isn't known yet), and Glow is never written back.
Photos edited before look exactly the same; effects only change a photo once you move a slider.

bugFixes: The Crop section's Reset now resets only the crop, angle, rotation and flip. Upright and the Transform sliders are kept; Transform has its own Reset.
Develop no longer briefly asks for an old thumbnail after you save and move to another photo (for example after Create Proof Copy), which used to log an error in the browser console.

newFeatures: Masking in Develop: adjust just part of a photo. A new Masks group offers Brush (K), Linear gradient (M), Radial gradient (Shift+M), Colour range (Shift+J) and Luminance range (Shift+Q).

Each mask has its own Temp, Tint, Exposure, Contrast, Highlights, Shadows, Whites, Blacks, Saturation and Vibrance, plus Feather and Refine. Combine brushes and gradients with Add, Subtract and Intersect, and invert any mask.
Colour and luminance range masks apply to the whole photo. To limit an adjustment to an area, use a brush or gradient mask.

See your masks with the overlay (O): Shift+O changes its colour and Alt+O its mode. Brush size is [ and ], feather { and }; hold Alt to erase. Pen pressure can change the brush size or flow (off by default).

Masks follow the photo when you change the crop, angle, Upright or lens corrections. They are saved in your library and in the photo's .xmp file, kept in snapshots and virtual copies, and included in exports.
Copy/Paste can include masks (unticked by default); pasted masks are added to the photo's own. Presets can hold gradient and range masks, but not brush strokes.

Masks made in Lightroom are read from the .xmp file when you import, as an experiment. When Lightroom kept its masks in a separate .acr file, LightBench tells you it can't read them. LightBench doesn't write masks for Lightroom.
Photos edited before look exactly the same.
Remove uses several processor cores to fill a spot, instead of one. The fills are exactly the same as before, so your edits don't change.

Exporting several photos is pipelined: while one photo is being saved as a JPEG, PNG or TIFF, the graphics card already develops the next, and several photos are encoded at once. The files are exactly the same as before.

LightBench's heavy background work shares half of your processor's cores. Work you're waiting for (Remove, Export, opening a folder) goes first; the culling measurements pause while an export runs and continue afterwards.
Export's Stop button now reads "Stop after the photos in progress": photos already developed are still saved.

Eyes for each section in Develop: besides each group's eye, you can now hide just one section to compare: Crop, Transform and Lens; White balance, Tone and Presence; the Tone Curve's Regions, RGB, Red, Green and Blue curves; Mixer and Point Color; each Colour Grading wheel; Sharpening and Noise reduction. Nothing is changed or saved, and the badge on the photo lists what is hidden.

Auto in the Tone Curve: Auto contrast fits a gentle S-curve to the photo without clipping more than before, and Auto colour makes small Red, Green and Blue curve corrections to remove a colour cast (white balance isn't touched). Both are ordinary curve points you can edit.
Curve suggestions: the curve presets and both Auto results are shown as small previews of your own photo. Hover to preview on the photo, click to apply.
Each Auto or suggestion is one step you can undo, with an Amount slider to dial it back.
bugFixes: Hiding Basic now shows the photo exactly as shot, including white balance on RAW files (it used to be a close approximation).
The eyes now reset when you move to another photo in Develop.

newFeatures: Soft proofing in Develop: press S (or tick Soft proofing in the toolbar) to preview how the photo will look in another colour space or on a printer. The preview changes only what you see; your edit and your exports stay the same.

Choose a profile: sRGB, an Adobe RGB (1998)-compatible profile and Display P3 are built in, and Load profile… adds your own .icc or .icm files (for example from your print lab). Loaded profiles stay on your computer and can be removed.

Choose the rendering intent: Relative Colorimetric with black point compensation is the default; Perceptual, Saturation and Absolute are available. Simulate Paper & Ink shows the paper's white and the ink's black.

Shift+S shows colours that fall outside the profile in red. The screen warning shows colours your display can't show in blue (based on sRGB or Display P3, because browsers don't tell the app which monitor profile you use); magenta means both. The histogram follows the proof.
Create Proof Copy makes a virtual copy named "Proof: <profile>" so you can adjust the photo for that output separately.
Colour conversion uses Little CMS, which starts only when you turn soft proofing on.

New Snapshots panel in Develop, above History: save the photo's current settings under a name (a date and time until you rename it) and go back to them at any time. Clicking a snapshot applies it as one step you can undo, and hovering one previews it.

Right-click a snapshot to update it with the current settings, rename it, delete it (Undo brings it back) or set it as the Before view (the \ key). Right-click a History step to make a snapshot from it.
Ctrl+Alt+N makes a snapshot. In the installed app window, Ctrl+N does too; in a browser tab, Ctrl+N still opens a new window as before.

Snapshots are kept in your library and in the photo's .xmp file, so they come back when you open the folder again, including in another copy of LightBench. Virtual copies have their own snapshots. Copy/Paste, Sync and presets don't carry them.
Photos edited before look exactly the same. Libraries are upgraded automatically; an older version of LightBench will no longer open an upgraded library.

Culling helpers in the Library: after a folder opens, LightBench measures each photo in the background (sharpness, camera shake, clipped exposure, look-alikes) and shows badges with the reason in their tooltips. Opening folders is as fast as before.

Sort and filter by sharpness, and "Select the best of each stack". Auto-stack can now group only photos that look alike, with a Strictness slider, and put the sharpest on top. Burst frames taken within the same second are now in the right order.

"Suggest rejects…" lists photos that are clearly softer than the best of their group, or shaken, with the reasons. Nothing is flagged until you press Apply, Undo puts the flags back, and no file is ever deleted.
In the culling view, Z zooms to the point the camera focused on (Sony and Fujifilm files so far), or to the sharpest area.

Settings › Culling has the badge switches, progress with Pause/Resume, and "Measure all photos again". Everything is measured on your computer and nothing is written to your photos or their .xmp files.

New Color Grading in Develop: Shadows, Midtones, Highlights and Global colour wheels, each with a Luminance slider, plus Blending and Balance, built on darktable's color balance rgb. Shift-drag changes saturation only, Ctrl-drag hue only, Alt-drag fine-tunes, and double-click resets a wheel.
Lightroom's Color Grading and older Split Toning settings are read from and written to its .xmp files.
Photos edited before look exactly the same; grading only changes a photo once you move a wheel.

bugFixes: System Check and Settings now show Adobe's DNG licence notice ("This product includes DNG technology under license by Adobe."), which Adobe's DNG patent licence asks for.

newFeatures: New Colour Mixer in Develop: Hue, Saturation and Luminance for eight colours (Red, Orange, Yellow, Green, Aqua, Blue, Purple, Magenta), built on darktable's color equalizer. Each colour blends smoothly into its neighbours without pushing other colours the wrong way, and greys stay neutral.
Point Color, a tab of the mixer: pick a colour on the photo and shift just that colour's hue, saturation and lightness, with range controls. Several points per photo.
Drag on the photo to adjust the colour under the pointer (Ctrl+Alt+Shift+H, S or L), and hold Alt while dragging a slider to see which areas it affects.
Lightroom's HSL / Color Mixer values are read from and written to its .xmp files. Point Color isn't exchanged with Lightroom yet, because its file format isn't documented.

New GPU benchmark in System Check: times each step of LightBench's processing (demosaic, lens and straighten, noise reduction, sharpening, display, Remove, export, thumbnails) on your own graphics card, with a Quick (about 30 seconds) and a Full mode.
Copy results gives a Markdown or JSON summary to share. Test images are generated on your computer, nothing is uploaded, and the benchmark waits while Develop or background work is busy.

If the graphics card stops responding, LightBench now recovers on its own: Develop rebuilds its view of the photo (unsaved changes kept), and Export, Paste/Sync and the 100 % view retry the photo once instead of asking you to reload the page.
Background work (Paste, Sync, presets, thumbnails, the 100 % view) now waits while Develop is busy, so editing stays responsive and less graphics memory is used at once.
bugFixes: Export no longer saves an all-black file when the graphics card runs out of memory or rejects the work. The photo is listed as failed with a plain explanation, and nothing is written.
Opening Develop while Paste or Sync was running could make the background work fail on some computers. Fixed.
Remove spot pins now always line up with the photo on screen, including right after rotating or cropping.

newFeatures: New Detail group in Develop. Sharpening (Amount, Radius, Detail, Masking) uses darktable's capture sharpening, which undoes the slight blur of the lens and sensor. Radius is a multiple of each photo's own measured blur, and holding Alt while dragging Masking shows which areas are sharpened.

Noise reduction (Luminance with Detail and Contrast, Color with Detail and Smoothness) uses darktable's denoise (profiled), with a noise profile for your camera and ISO when darktable has one. The profiles download the first time you use noise reduction, then work offline.
New RAW photos are lightly sharpened (Amount 40, or 25 above ISO 1000). Noise reduction stays off until you turn it up. Photos you edited before look exactly as they did.
Lightroom's Sharpening and Noise Reduction values are read from and written to its .xmp files, under the same rules as the other Lightroom settings.

New Tone Curve group in Develop, after Basic (Curve on the jump bar). Shape the look with Regions (Highlights, Lights, Darks, Shadows and three split points) or point curves for RGB, Red, Green and Blue, with Linear, Medium Contrast, Strong Contrast and Fade presets.
Colours keep their hue as the curve changes contrast, and get stronger where it gets steeper, like Lightroom. The Refine Saturation slider takes that colour boost back (0 % changes brightness only).
A targeted adjustment tool: drag up or down on the photo to bend the curve at that tone. The graph shows the photo's histogram behind the curve and marks where it clips to pure white or black.
Tone curves made in Lightroom are read from the photo's .xmp file, and a curve you change in LightBench is written back to .xmp files that already hold Lightroom settings.
New Remove brush (Q): paint over dust, wires or small objects and LightBench fills them from their surroundings, no AI. Each spot can be switched to Heal or Clone, and its source dragged elsewhere.
Spots stay on the same place in the photo through crop, rotation, Upright and lens correction, and every export gets exactly the same fill.
Copy/Paste and Sync can carry Remove, Heal & Clone spots to other photos at the same place on the sensor (for sensor dust); off by default.
On Fujifilm X-Trans photos, Develop › Advanced › Demosaic now offers darktable's Markesteijn 3-pass (slower). Markesteijn 1-pass stays the default, so existing edits don't change.
bugFixes: The sensor-clipping overlay (Shift+O) now lines up with the photo near the corners when lens corrections are on.

newFeatures: New process version 2: Highlights, Shadows, Whites and Blacks now work like darktable's tone equalizer. Each area is brightened or darkened by its surroundings, so fine detail and local contrast are kept and edges no longer get pale fringes.
Photos edited before keep their look. Use “Update to current process” in Develop to move them to version 2; its tooltip says what changes. Photos with the four tone sliders at 0 look the same.
Crops, straightening, rotation and flips made in Lightroom now appear in LightBench, read from the photo's .xmp file.

A crop or rotation you change in LightBench is written back to Lightroom's own fields in .xmp files that already hold Lightroom settings. Lightroom's other settings are left exactly as they were, and opening a photo never rewrites them.

An Upright setting from Lightroom is redone with LightBench's own Upright, which may differ slightly from Lightroom's; the Transform section says so. Guided Upright lines from Lightroom can't be imported.
If you change a crop in Lightroom, LightBench notices, and Read changes brings it in.
bugFixes: After the graphics card resets, Paste, Sync and other background developing start again instead of failing for every remaining photo.

newFeatures: Export: new Output sharpening (Sharpen for Screen, Matte paper or Glossy paper; Low, Standard or High), off by default. It sharpens only the exported file after resizing, and adapts to the print resolution or to how much the photo is downsized.
Export: new Resolution setting (pixels per inch, default 300) under Size, written into the exported file.
] and [ give a photo one star more or less, and Shift+0–5 sets the rating and moves to the next photo, as in Lightroom (Library, culling, Compare and Survey).

Photos added before 0.4.0 now get their GPS location and, if their camera preview is Adobe RGB, thumbnails with correct colours, once, in the background (with Pause); edited photos, ratings and sidecars are left as they are.
bugFixes: On keyboards with accented letters (German Ü, Ö, Ä; French é, è, ç, à), those keys no longer act as the US key in the same place (e.g. Ctrl+Ä made a virtual copy).
Virtual copies now keep their photo's GPS location.

newFeatures: Lens corrections: distortion, chromatic aberration and dark corners are corrected with the camera's own data (Sony, and Fujifilm, Olympus, DNG and Panasonic as darktable reads them) or a Lensfun profile. On for new photos; earlier edits stay as they were until you tick Lens corrections.
The Lens section (in Crop & Lens) shows which data corrected the photo, lets you pick the camera or lens when the match is wrong, and has Distortion and Vignetting amounts.
Lensfun's lens data is downloaded the first time a photo needs it, then works offline.

Transform: Upright Auto, Level, Vertical and Full straighten leaning buildings and tilted horizons in one click, using darktable's line detection and the photo's focal length; when the lines found aren't reliable, the photo is left alone and LightBench says why.
Guided Upright (Shift+T): draw 2–4 lines along edges that should be vertical or horizontal; drag their ends to adjust, Delete removes one.
Transform sliders: Vertical, Horizontal, Rotate, Aspect, Scale and X/Y Offset. The photo is enlarged so no empty corners show.
Auto straighten in the crop group (or double-click with Level on) levels the photo along the lines it finds.
Paste, Sync and presets: Upright Auto, Level, Vertical and Full are detected again on each photo; the Transform sliders are copied as they are.
A JPEG shot alongside a RAW now keeps its own sidecar (IMG_1.JPG.xmp), so the two no longer share stars and edits.
Thumbnails and previews of RAWs shot in Adobe RGB show their real colours instead of looking washed out.
Where a photo was taken (GPS) is read from RAWs and JPEGs and shown in the Library's info panel.
Title, caption, creator, copyright, location and keywords written by older apps (IPTC) are read from JPEGs.
On wide-gamut (Display P3) screens, Develop shows colours beyond sRGB.
Fujifilm X-Trans RAW files (RAF) now open, develop and export, with darktable's Markesteijn demosaic.
Linear DNGs (Apple ProRAW and other phone or converter DNGs) now open, develop and export, using the colour matrices stored in the file.
bugFixes: Extreme Tint or Temp settings on a JPEG no longer turn its colours inside out (e.g. Tint +150).
Phone DNGs whose camera LibRaw doesn't know (e.g. Google Pixel) no longer fail with “Matrix is not invertible”.

newFeatures: Crop and straighten (R): drag corners or edges, drag inside to move, drag outside to turn the photo under a level crop box. Enter applies, Esc cancels.
Crop aspects Original, 1:1, 4:5, 5:7, 2:3, 16:9 and Custom, with a lock; X swaps portrait and landscape; O cycles thirds, grid, golden ratio and diagonals.
Straighten with the Angle slider, or draw a level line along the horizon (the Level button, or Ctrl-drag while cropping).
Rotate left and right (Ctrl+[ and Ctrl+]) and flip horizontally or vertically.
The crop is used everywhere: histogram, Auto, thumbnails, Export, 100 % views, and Paste, Sync and presets (tick Crop to copy it).
Develop's tools are now one scrolling list with a jump bar (Crop, Basic); groups can be closed, and an eye shows the photo without a group.
Process versions: each edit remembers which version of LightBench's rendering it uses, so later changes never alter it until you choose “Update to current process”.
Back up the whole library (catalog, thumbnails and settings) to one checked file, and restore it safely.
LightBench notices when Lightroom, darktable or another app changes a photo's sidecar, and asks before overwriting it.
bugFixes: Star ratings changed in Lightroom or Bridge are no longer overridden when LightBench re-reads the sidecar.
Keywords that other apps store only as plain (flat) keywords are no longer dropped.
Photos copied from a card are now checked byte-for-byte; a bad copy is reported instead of being added.
A library saved by a newer LightBench is refused untouched, with a Reload button.
Notices when the browser may clear the library, or when a save fails.

newFeatures: Compare (C): the photo you like best stays on the left while the arrow keys bring in others to compare with it.
Survey (N): the selected photos side by side, to flag, rate and drop them until the best are left.
Metadata: edit title, caption, creator, copyright and location on one photo or many. They are saved in sidecars and included in exports.
Metadata presets (“© {year} Your Name” becomes each photo's year) that can fill in new photos, and import presets for the Import window's options.
Settings (the gear, or Ctrl+,): change any keyboard shortcut, or switch to Lightroom Classic's keys.
Press ? for the shortcuts of the current view, or Ctrl+Shift+P to find any action by name.
Interface size from 90 % to 150 % (Ctrl+Alt+= and Ctrl+Alt+−). Photos stay sharp.
Choose the background behind photos: black, dark grey or mid grey.
Develop sliders: arrow keys nudge, Shift+arrows take bigger steps, Home resets.
Install LightBench as an app from Chrome or Edge (the install button in the address bar).
Works offline after the first visit. Your photos and library were already stored on your computer.
An “Update ready” notice with these notes. Nothing changes until you click Reload.
Open RAW and JPEG files with the installed app from your file manager (Chrome and Edge).
Copy, paste and sync develop settings between photos, choosing which settings go. Auto can re-run on each photo.
Auto options: a strength slider and a choice of which sliders Auto may change.
Presets: save chosen settings, preview on hover, apply with an Amount, and develop new photos with one automatically.
